payload: Every host serves one API at fnPath. A board's address is the first 24 hex chars of the sha-256 of its pairing code; possession of the id is read AND write (writes travel with the id as x-rc-key). The relay carries the extension's own board webview: the page is media/board.js verbatim behind a bridge, the extension pushes the frames it would post to that webview, and the page queues the messages that webview would post back. GET ?id=<boardId>[&since=<seq>][&d=1][&wait=<secs>] returns { ok, seq, at, writes, mv, frame?, deltas?, events[] } — frame (the latest composed { type:'state', state } with state.composer.models split out) only when it is newer than since; deltas (frame patches, oldest first) INSTEAD of frame when the caller passed d=1 and the retained chain reaches its cursor, and never on a first load; events (host-to-page messages: searchResults, mentions, voice, remote dialogs and toasts) newer than since, at most eventsMax retained; wait is honoured only by hosts that can hold a request. GET ?id=<boardId>&models=1 returns { ok, mv, models[] }; GET ?id=<boardId>&msgs=1[&wait=<secs>] returns { ok, msgs[], viewerAt } — with wait, a host that can hold a request holds it until the queue is non-empty or the timeout, so a pushing machine learns of a queued message as it lands rather than at its next tick; every GET answer from such a host carries longPoll:true and a caller must never assume holding without it. POST { kind:'frame', at, writes, mv, state?, patch?, models? } answers { ok, patches:true, frameSeq, mv, viewerAt, msgs[], needFrame? }: state REPLACES the frame and clears the patch ring; patch = { base, state, rows?:{ from, rows[] } } is COMPOSED onto the held frame — state is the board without its transcript and rows replaces the transcript from `from` onwards — and is refused with needFrame:true when base is not the held frameSeq or the splice would leave a gap, so the pusher sends a whole state next; neither present = heartbeat, at only; at most deltasMax patches are retained. patches:true is how a pusher learns the relay understands patch frames — it is never assumed. POST { kind:'event', events[] } appends host-to-page events; POST { kind:'msg', nonce, msg:{ type, ... } } queues one webview message for the pushing machine — msg.type matches typeOk, the JSON is at most msgMaxBytes, at most msgMax queued — and whether it runs is the extension's decision (remote.writes), never the relay's; POST { kind:'ack', nonces[] } removes acked messages (at-least-once). Requests are serialised per board id, because every branch is a read-modify-write. The static page and all three hosts (Netlify functions, Cloudflare Worker, plain Node) speak exactly this.
